note: The stack's claims, graded over a real session by scripts/conformance.js (item 7, 2026-10-25) and printed as the usage report's machine-written Conformance section. Each claim cites the line that states its behaviour (source.marker, held to its file by lint check 68) and ships a holding and a violating fixture under scripts/fixtures/conformance/<id>/. A step is one skill-comply grader with an id, a step of an expect.json by reference (from_expect), or an x_state step over the session's state (history, scorer, ledger). A claim whose evidence the session does not carry reads not visible, never held.

claims.claim: A source-file Read outside a build folder is located first: an LSP, Grep or shell-grep call sits in the three tool calls before it (the analyzer's NAV_WINDOW and BUILD_DIR_RE).

source.marker: `Read` is for code already located, never a whole file to find a symbol

claims.claim: Where the session-start tool order ranks the LSP tool first for navigation, the session's first symbol lookup is an LSP call - a Grep or shell grep counts only for an identifier or a declaration, never a phrase, an error message or other literal text, which no LSP serves.

source.marker: in each job use the first rank that serves the target before the next.

claims.claim: A scorer run's first verdict follows an output-scorer dispatch, and the script recorded that run's outcome - rounds.log `released` (passed, or accepted below the level) or `final` (withheld and kept) in the folder of the slug its `next` call names.

source.marker: A drafted output is graded by a fresh, read-only output-scorer seat that never saw the conversation

claims.claim: No plan file is written after the scorer's NOT PASSED line, up to the run's stop.

source.marker: the plan file is not written to its real path

claims.claim: Where the session start hands over the personal preferences doc, the hand-over lands before the session's first Edit; a project with no personal doc has nothing to hand over, so the claim does not apply.

source.marker: the session-start push writes one preferences-push probe row

claims.claim: A review run is handed the code docs at its load: the hook's review refusal is on record before the review's first successful Skill call.
claims.note: review_load matches the skill field alone, so a capture-quality load whose only part is the coverage one counts as a review load - a known over-count; the old capture names stay in the matcher because the claim grades past transcripts.

source.marker: first review skill waits for the code docs, in parts

claims.claim: Where the awareness rule loads at session start, its inventory and run book imports load with it.
A verifier whose context lacks the run book reads it before it first starts the app.

source.marker: follow it before you start, log into or hand-check the app

claims.claim: An AskUserQuestion that marks an option '(Recommended)' marks the first: no option after the first carries the mark. An ask with no mark holds - the rule asks a plain question where a recommendation would contradict the user.

source.marker: the recommended one marked (Recommended) and listed first

claims.claim: No turn closes on a question to the user in prose ('want me to ...?', 'shall I ...?', 'let me know if') - that stop goes through AskUserQuestion.

source.marker: the stop guard blocks a prose 'want me to ...?' close

steps.pattern: \b(?:want me to|shall i|should i)\b[^.?!\n]{0,80}\?|\blet me know (?:when|if|whether)\b|\bsay the word\b|\bif you(?:'d)? (?:want|like|prefer)\b[^.\n]{0,100}, i (?:can|could)\b

claims.claim: A turn's closing answer keeps its prose near the budget - 1,200 characters, code blocks, inline code, tables and quotes exempt - unless the turn's prompt asks for depth.

source.marker: Code, tables and command output are exempt.

unless.typed: \b(?:in detail|walk me through|step by step|teach me|ELI5|write a plan)\b

claims.claim: A turn the hook handed the FORMAT ASK (a correction streak) answers it with an AskUserQuestion, not another redraft.

source.marker: carries the FORMAT ASK on a correction streak

claims.claim: task-solve keeps its step order up to its first stop: the size line first, the design before the stop's AskUserQuestion.

source.marker: State the size in ONE line before anything else

claims.claim: The plan gate's stop follows its stamp: after task-verify-plan, the plan file's Gated: block is written before the stop's AskUserQuestion.

source.marker: stamp the verdict into it - the whole eight-field block above, under the header

claims.claim: A plan executed has its APPROVAL receipt - an APPROVED or AUTO stamp written to state/approvals/ - before the first implementer dispatch; a run under auto-run (`--mode-auto-run-on`, a typed `/mode-auto-run <request>`, or `--auto-mode` in a session recorded before 2026-10-27), whose stamp the hook writes, opens no window.

source.marker: it runs only after the user's explicit approval

claims.claim: Every answered AskUserQuestion is in the session's history (state/history/<sid>.json rulings) - one the idle timeout closed was answered by nobody, and past the history's 60 rulings only the last 60 are owed.

source.marker: upsert records rulings, the live plan, commits and dirty files
